ad_intro: Araku Coffee is the largest advertiser in this batch by creative volume: approximately 200 live creatives under Araku Originals Pvt Ltd (verified), spanning Shopping, Local and video formats. The account runs a Moka Pot and a Chemex Coffee Maker as Product Listing Ads alongside store listings with directions and reserve actions — a blend of e-commerce and café marketing in one advertiser. The measurement base is in place (GA4, Google Ads, Clarity, Razorpay). The defect is a feed setting: every Shopping click is tagged utm_campaign=sag_organic, so paid traffic is filed as organic traffic in analytics, and at this creative volume that is a lot of spend being reported as free.

findings: Every Shopping click is being filed under 'sag_organic': The feed is tagging paid Shopping traffic with the campaign name 'sag_organic'. In GA4 that traffic is reported as organic, so the account cannot see what Shopping actually earns — and at roughly two hundred creatives, that is a lot of spend being reported as free. Fixing the feed's tracking template is a minutes-long change with immediate effect on every report the team reads.

The storefront's URL structure is non-standard, so conventional links break: Ad destinations observed in the archive are product URLs, which work — so paid traffic is safe. The risk is everything off-campaign: press coverage, retail partners, café signage and customers typing obvious addresses. Standard redirects from the conventional handles to the real ones remove that risk permanently.

Café and e-commerce are running in the same account without separation: Two very different businesses — a café visit and a packaged-coffee order — share one advertiser account and one set of conversion actions. Unless the café and the store have separate conversion definitions, the account cannot tell whether a rupee of spend bought a cup or a bag, which makes budget decisions between them arbitrary.

On Meta, the brand term is being crowded by other businesses: A distinctive brand name is an asset, and it is being spent by others on Meta: a partner using the name in a workshop promotion and a similarly named café in another state. Neither is hostile and neither is confirmed as a problem — but it does mean brand-term searches on Meta return someone else's business before yours, and that is worth a look at the account level.

Razorpay and a clean tag base are in place across the store: The measurement base and the payment stack are in place, and the entity disclosure on the site matches the verified advertiser — which is exactly what a brand with a co-operative origin story needs in order to be credible. The work here is in reporting hygiene, not rebuilding.
competitors: Araku's seed-to-cup and plantation story is stronger; the paid account has the volume to tell it, the reporting just cannot see it clearly.
Araku is already bidding there — separate those campaigns from the café so both can be judged.
Third parties using the brand name
Ride the brand's search equity on Meta.
Worth a look at the account level to see whether partner placements are intended.
wins: WIN 1 - Fix the sag_organic campaign tag
Minutes in the feed settings; until then every Shopping click is reported as organic traffic.
WIN 2 - Separate café and e-commerce conversions
Two conversion actions, two views of spend, a defensible budget split between the store and the cafés.
WIN 3 - Add redirects from the conventional handles
contact-us, about-us, faq, menu and locations should land on the pages that exist — for every third-party and printed link in circulation.
